A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a multi-channel channel-adaptive scheme for image coding in a noisy transmission channel, and that the scheme has been shown to be optimal under a given set of assumptions.
a block-based modification for the EZW coding scheme is applied to improve its robustness, and the resultant coded bitstreams are used in the rate-distortions analysis.
we have successfully developed a multi-channel channel optimized scheme for image compression, which has been verified by computer simulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bitstream produced for a noisy channel should be more robust to noise, and that the bit allocation should be done in the rate-distoration sense, taking the channel noise into account.

the bit allocation can be performed based on the rate-distortion functions, which are derived from the channel noise statistics, and the bitstream produced by the channel-optimized scheme is more robust than that by a single-channel scheme, which is optimized for a specific noise level.
, by considering the channel noise in rate-distortion analysis and optimal bit allocation, the performance of the multi-channel channel-optimization scheme is significantly improved.
